title: Inverse Learning of the Altruism and Cost Level in Mixed-Individual Mean Field Games
summary: Understanding how humans respond to incentives, both at the individual and collective levels, is crucial to the design of effective policies. Within the continuous-time stochastic framework for large interacting populations, mean field games (MFGs) model populations of non-cooperative agents, whereas mean field control (MFC) describes the fully cooperative benchmark, interpreted in our setting as fully altruistic behavior. Mixed-individual MFGs interpolate between these two extremes through a parameter governing the degree of altruism. A central challenge for regulators and policymakers,…
